$comment: Machine-readable harness catalogue. The behavioural source of truth is tools/slice-agent-runner/src/harnesses.ts; the installer's HARNESS_IDS and docs/harnesses.md mirror the same ids, and tests/test_harness_catalogue.py fails when they drift apart. Invocations were checked against vendor docs on verified_on; flags move between releases, so the vendor docs win.

harnesses.name: Claude Code
harnesses.notes: -p prints and exits. --permission-mode acceptEdits lets it write files without prompting; dontAsk is the locked-down CI variant. Checked against vendor documentation, not executed here.

harnesses.name: Codex CLI
harnesses.notes: exec runs headless; workspace-write permits edits without network. Upstream deprecated --full-auto in favour of the explicit sandbox flag. Checked against vendor documentation, not executed here.

harnesses.name: Cursor CLI
harnesses.notes: Print mode without --force only proposes changes. Some installations expose the binary as `agent`. Checked against vendor documentation, not executed here.

harnesses.name: Cline
harnesses.notes: Verified by running cline 3.0.68's --help (positional prompt, --auto-approve <boolean>, --plan, --json, --timeout). Pin the version: npm i -g cline@3.0.68. If the binary does not appear, check that npm's global bin directory is on PATH, and on npm versions that gate install scripts allow them for this package. Upstream flagged old versions as malicious, so pinning is not optional.

harnesses.name: Aider
harnesses.notes: Verified by running aider 0.86.2's --help: --message-file, --yes-always and --no-auto-commits all exist as written.

harnesses.name: Any harness (bring your own command)
harnesses.notes: Runs through a shell, so Cline, Goose, OpenHands, a custom script or a wrapper around your own tooling all plug in here.
